name: Freya Rossi

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What happens in a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the disputed-card call row for a regional bank's contact centre called Meridian Cards. When someone says a payment isn't theirs, I check the merchant, time and card history before placing a hold. I have a two-year college diploma and am good at stopping a second bad charge, though I earn ordinary pay, not some special security wage.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does a difficult call sound like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Often it is a person frightened they cannot buy groceries while a card is blocked. The AI note finder sometimes saves me a search, but I still check the ledger myself. My partner Joel works regular paid shifts in a bakery, our grown children live on their own, and we have about five months of expenses saved.

say: I would keep **human checks** on disputed charges.
I would use **faster note search** without skipping the ledger.
think: I expect my **hard-call wage** to stay steady while people still need disputed-card explanations.
I need **verified later income** before reducing hours, despite five months saved.
do: Keep **paid dispute calls** and verify suggested notes against the ledger.
Save a **small fixed pay amount** only when rent and food remain covered.
feel: **Calm** with regular wages and a five-month buffer.
S0.quote: Blocking the wrong card can leave someone at the shop till with no way to pay.
fieldNote: She uses AI **occasionally** for notes, not to make a final fraud decision.
The five-month **reserve** and regular bakery pay support a calm mild scenario.
Her savings addition is **conditional** on rent and food remaining paid.

steps.text: Keep paid disputed-card calls and check suggested notes against ledger entries
Transfer small fixed pay amount to separate reserve only after rent and food are covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a faster search of card notes is useful if we still check a disputed charge ourselves. Blocking the wrong card can leave someone at the shop till with no way to pay. I would keep a person on those calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the hard dispute calls and my pay stay steady in this mild version. Five months saved and Joel's regular bakery wage give us a reasonable buffer. I still want written figures before deciding what income we could live on if either of us worked less later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my paid dispute row and check any suggested note against the ledger as I do now. This year Joel and I would put a small fixed amount from normal pay into a separate reserve whenever rent and food are covered. In the first year of this mild picture I would keep the same rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. There is enough paid work today and money behind us for a bad month. I would still do the later-life figures before calling any date a retirement plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you check before blocking a card?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the merchant number and amount match a known subscription, I can explain that before freezing a card. If they do not, I follow the bank's fraud procedure. The customer needs an answer they can use at the till.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children be part of your later-income plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown children can visit, but their pay belongs to them. Joel and I would use our own wages and verified later-income figures. We would not ask them to promise us an allowance.

say: I would require **correctable AI alerts** before a card stays blocked.
I would ask for **paid customer access** when a dispute needs a person.
think: Routine automation could shrink my **paid dispute row**.
I can learn **new alert controls** after the first team tests them.
do: After the first fraud team tests it, attend **approved paid AI training** and practise three false blocks.
Keep **paid dispute calls** and record blocked customers without correction.
After hour cuts, compare **posted branch rotas** before applying; move only if weekly wages/hours after travel cover rent and bills.
feel: **Anxious** about paid hours despite a five-month buffer.
S1.quote: A branch badge by itself is not a wage.
fieldNote: She waits for the first team to **prove the alert tool** before learning its new controls.
Her move depends on **full-week wages and hours** after travel.
She does not mistake a **trainer title** for protected paid hours.

steps.text: After first fraud-team test, attend approved paid AI alert-triage demonstration and practise three false blocks
Keep paid dispute calls and record failed customer corrections
Compare posted branch rotas after own hour cuts by full-week wages, hours and travel
Move only if branch weekly wages and hours after travel cover rent and bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the bank that a faster alert is welcome if a person can still correct it before a customer's card is blocked. We should see what happened to real disputed charges during a trial. I do not want 'efficiency' to mean a frightened customer gets a bot loop instead of a paid agent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Routine disputes may move to the new system and reduce our paid row. I can learn an alert tool once the first team proves it, but I cannot assume a trainer title will keep my hours. Five months saved would buy a search, not replace a steady wage forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask to join the approved paid demonstration after the first fraud team has tested the new AI alert-triage screen, then practise checking three false blocks. I'd keep my paid dispute calls and record where a customer could not get a correction. If my own hours actually fall over the next few years, I'd compare the posted local branch rotas by complete weekly wages and hours after travel before applying; in the first year I'd keep paid calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a smaller paid row, although I like seeing a tool proved before I use it. I have a buffer and some branches nearby. I still need a full weekly wage for our rent and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn in the demonstration?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The new screen shows why it stopped a card and lets an authorised agent reopen it. I would learn that control on three false blocks after the first team has tried it. I will not treat a demonstration as proof that customers can always reach someone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would a branch job be worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check the actual posted hours and pay before applying. I would move only if full-week wages and hours after travel cover our rent and bills. A branch badge by itself is not a wage.

say: I would warn **2028 thinking AI** reaches card disputes before robots.
I would ask for **real paid branch rotas** before a move.
think: I expect most **dispute calls** to end soon after 2028.
I know five months saved cannot replace a **long-term wage**.
do: List **posted branch openings** by weekly wages, hours, travel, duties and required security training before taking a shift.
Apply if row ends in 2028-29 to a **paid counter**; accept only rent/bill-covering weekly wages/hours after travel.
Keep **remaining paid calls** during a bounded savings-funded search.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected pay loss and uncertain branch hiring.
S2.quote: I would lose sleep if nearby branches froze hiring at the same time.
fieldNote: Her moderate **five-month reserve** buys time but not lasting wages.
Branch roles may face **AI and robots** at different dates too.
She checks posted **security duties** before accepting counter work.

steps.text: Check posted branch and cashier openings by wages, hours, travel and security training before taking shift
Apply if row ends in 2028-29 to paid counter; accept rent/bill-covering weekly wages/hours after travel
Keep available paid calls while using bounded existing savings for search

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say full thinking AI by 2028 could read the card record and reassure a customer more cheaply than the call row. Robots around 2031 do not give the headset extra time. A branch counter may last a little longer, but I would ask for a real paid rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect Meridian Cards to end most disputed-card calls in the first year after 2028, perhaps closing my row. Five months saved gives us a search window, but Joel's bakery pay alone does not cover the whole household. I would lose sleep if nearby branches froze hiring at the same time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd list the actual posted branch and cashier openings within bus reach, including weekly wages, hours and travel costs. If my dispute row ends in the first year after 2028, I'd apply to a real paid branch counter opening. I'd accept only if the full paid week after travel covers rent and bills; otherwise I'd keep available paid calls and use a bounded share of savings to search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I can make a plan for five months, but I expect a big wage loss and might not find another paid week before the reserve runs down. That would keep me awake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why inspect branch counters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A counter can involve cash, identity checks and customers face to face. Thinking AI may do some of that, and robots around 2031 may change physical tasks too. I would check the posted duties and security training before taking a shift, not assume a branch is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can Joel's bakery pay carry the household?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Joel would keep the bakery hours he actually has, but we would compare his weekly payslips with rent instead of guessing. Our children have their own homes. Their wages are not a bridge we can budget.

say: I would request a **paid branch shadow shift** for a posted role.
I would reject a **course without paid work** behind it.
think: I could test **branch customer help** while call wages continue.
I know **2031 AGI** may reach harder screen checks too.
do: Request one **paid branch shadow shift** for a posted opening; complete security induction before taking it.
Keep **paid dispute calls**, list branch hours quarterly and recheck cashier rota without opening, using bounded existing savings for search.
Apply after 2031 closure only for **rent-and-bill-covering weekly wages/hours** after travel.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect actual work and paid hours.
S3.quote: I would rather see a paid branch rota than a glossy training leaflet.
fieldNote: The paid shadow shift requires a **posted opening** and bank security induction.
She keeps **current calls** while paid, even as she checks branch work.
No suitable branch role means **paid calls** and cashier search continue.

steps.text: Request paid branch shadow shift for posted opening; complete security induction before taking it
Keep paid dispute calls and list actual posted branch hours quarterly
Apply if row closes in 2031-32 only to posted rent/bill-covering weekly wages/hours after travel
Without branch opening, keep paid calls, check cashier rota quarterly and search using bounded existing savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years is enough to test whether the bank will pay people to handle customers stranded by a false fraud alert. We do not need another certificate if there is no posted work behind it. I would rather see a paid branch rota than a glossy training leaflet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build on my card-dispute experience and try a branch customer-help shift while calls still pay. Full AGI in 2031 may handle even the harder screen checks, and a branch is not a permanent shield. The extra years matter because I can compare a real paid week before I leave this one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I'd ask to shadow an experienced branch worker on one paid shift if a posted customer-help opening exists. I'd keep my paid dispute rota and list the actual branch hours each quarter. In the first year after 2031, if the call row closes, I'd apply for that posted paid opening only if weekly wages and hours after travel cover rent and bills; without a suitable opening I'd stay on any paid calls and check the cashier rota again.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but less rushed than with two years. A paid shift would show me whether I can handle the counter rules. It would not promise the bank will keep that role after AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check on a shadow shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask who is authorised to check identity and how an agent handles someone whose card is blocked. I will not take a counter shift without the bank's safety and security induction. The trial has to be paid, because my current shift already pays bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no branch opening is posted?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the dispute calls that remain paid and compare the posted cashier work each quarter. I would not pay for a speculative course. Joel and I can use part of the reserve for a bounded search, not an open-ended gap.

I would say **2036 thinking AI** reaches disputes before later robots change branch work.
think: I may still need **paid work at sixty-eight** if verified later income is short.
I see five months saved as **search room**, not a retirement wage.
do: Keep **paid dispute calls** and check written later-income figures against bills.
Apply if row ends in 2036-37 only for **rent-and-bill-covering weekly wages/hours** after travel.
feel: **Uneasy** about unverified later income, with a five-month buffer.
S4.quote: I would rather check our later-income figures now than find a rent gap at sixty-eight.
fieldNote: She ties the **income check** to the annual rent review.
The reserve offers time, not **guaranteed retirement pay**.
She keeps **paid hours** if later-income figures cannot cover bills.

steps.text: Keep paid dispute calls and compare written later income with actual rent and wages
Review posted branch jobs each autumn by full-week wages and hours
Apply if row ends in 2036-37 only to rent/bill-covering weekly wages/hours after travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade is long enough to get real work and income figures rather than guess. Thinking AI could reach dispute calls by 2036, and robots might change branch tasks around 2039. I would want a paid rota in front of me before changing jobs or hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At sixty-eight I might still need wages; Joel and I have not verified income that would replace our current pay. Five months saved is useful, but it is not a retirement wage. A long warning could make it too easy to delay the paperwork until the pay stops.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year Joel and I would get written figures for any later income and compare them with rent, bills and actual wages. I'd keep the paid dispute row and look at posted local branch jobs each autumn. If the call row ends in the first year after 2036, I'd apply only to work whose complete weekly wages and hours after travel cover the household bills; if later income is too small, I'd keep paid work in our plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. We can handle several bad months with the reserve, but I cannot set a date to stop work without real figures. I would rather check our later-income figures now than find a rent gap at sixty-eight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you avoid delaying the figures?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd attach the income check to our annual rent review. If the figures show fewer shifts are affordable, we can talk about that. If they do not, I'll keep the paid hours I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children help if income is short?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They are welcome for Sunday lunch, but our grown children have budgets of their own. We would not put their wages in the plan. Joel and I will check the written figures ourselves.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The two-year one worries me most because the dispute row could close before a branch has a paid week ready. A posted role with real wages, hours and security induction would help. Five months saved buys a search, not a second career.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens when a customer is falsely blocked at the grocery till. A refund next week does not buy dinner tonight. I want that case to stay somebody's paid responsibility.

headlineQuote: A refund next week does not buy dinner tonight.
portrait: Freya is a **58-year-old** disputed-card lead with a two-year college diploma.
She earns **typical pay** and has five months of expenses saved.
She uses AI **sometimes** and learns new tools after a first team tests them.
She considers **paid branch work** only after checking posted hours and security duties.
She will not assume **later-life income** or support from grown children.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028**, when the dispute row may close before another paid week exists.
whatWouldHelp: A **posted paid branch rota** with full weekly wages, hours and security induction.
